newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front to pick leader on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front to pick leader on Saturday.

text.p: India's defeated United Front coalition said on Friday it had postponed a scheduled meeting to elect a new leader to replace Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda till Saturday.
"The Steering Committee has postponed its meeting until Saturday," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told Reuters.
United Front officials said the alliance's Convener Chandrababu Naidu, whom the group has authorised to name a new leader, had met with senior members of the 15-party coalition on Friday.

Friday's scheduled meeting of the decision-making Steering Committee was postponed because Deve Gowda was delayed in the eastern state of Orissa while returning from the funeral of a senior leader of his Janata Dal party who died on Thursday.
United Front officials said the choice of a new leader would be determined by his ability to lead the 15-party alliance to elections which they fear are imminent.

There was growing consensus within the coalition on naming a leader from the populous northern Hindi-speaking region where the United Front faces the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party as its chief rival, the official said.
